answer: Paragraph 14 most naturally attaches “upon SFC’s request” to demonstration, leaving confirmation unconditioned by a request. Both concern management and operational soundness, ownership record keeping and smart-contract integrity; demonstration expressly must satisfy the SFC. Footnote 5 specifies minimum content for both confirmation and demonstration, but omits the request condition, creating a supported rival reading of a standing demonstration requirement. Without a request, confirmation remains expected; demonstration is untriggered under the main-text and integrated readings, but remains expected under the standing-footnote reading. Paragraphs 15 and 16 separately condition obtaining third-party audit or verification, and a satisfactory legal opinion, on the relevant SFC request. None of these trigger conclusions establishes fulfillment.

claims.inference: Text and grammatical deduction: the inserted request phrase immediately precedes “demonstrate”; “to the SFC’s satisfaction” most naturally qualifies demonstration. This does not supply a separate sufficiency test for confirmation.
missing_premises: Applicability of the retained edition to the entity, product, activity and assessment period, including any specific conditions or modifications.
claims.proposition: Paragraph 14 supports confirmation without a request and request-triggered demonstration concerning the same three subjects, with demonstration expressly subject to the SFC’s satisfaction.

support.quote: Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

claims.inference: Text: footnote 5 addresses both verbs, expressly identifies the SFC as recipient, and adds minimum content. “With a high level of confidence” most naturally concerns the absence of smart-contract vulnerabilities or security flaws; the supplied text gives no numerical threshold. Reading the footnote as content clarification preserves paragraph 14’s request trigger; reading its unqualified demonstration wording independently supports a competing standing duty.
missing_premises: An authoritative resolution of the relationship between the main-text request condition and the footnote’s unqualified wording.
An applicable evidential standard for high confidence and SFC satisfaction.
claims.proposition: Footnote 5 requires, as minimum confirmation and demonstration content, compliance with paragraphs 10–13 and assurance concerning smart-contract vulnerabilities and security flaws with a high level of confidence; its trigger attachment remains disputed.
claims.status: Content textually supported; trigger interpretation unresolved

support.quote: Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.
upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction

claims.inference: Conditional deduction: assuming no applicable request was made, the main-text trigger is absent. That leaves confirmation and underlying substantive requirements intact. Under the rival standing-footnote reading, demonstration remains expected. Missing evidence of a request is not itself proof that none exists.
missing_premises: Actual request history and the scope and timing of any SFC communications.
Selection and justification of the governing interpretation.
Actual confirmation, operational, ownership-record and smart-contract evidence measured against an applicable standard.
claims.proposition: No request means no triggered demonstration requirement under readings A and C, but does not establish compliance, excuse confirmation or remove the underlying requirements; reading B yields a different demonstration result.
claims.status: Conditional deduction, not a fulfillment finding

Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC

Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

claims.inference: Text and deduction: paragraph 15 conditions obtaining external audit or verification on a request. Its object overlaps paragraph 14’s subjects, but the required act differs from confirmation or demonstration. A communication may cover several paragraphs, but its scope must establish each relevant request; one cannot automatically substitute for another.
missing_premises: An applicable request covering paragraph 15 audit or verification.
The requested scope, applicable quality standard and evidence that a qualifying audit or verification was obtained.
claims.proposition: Paragraph 15 provides a separate request-triggered expectation to obtain third-party audit or verification; it does not expressly repeat paragraph 14’s SFC-satisfaction standard.

support.quote: Product Providers should, upon SFC’s request, obtain third party audit or verification on the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and integrity of the smart contracts.

claims.inference: Text and deduction: the request qualifies obtaining the opinion, whose object is support for the application. “Satisfactory” is express, but this sentence does not identify detailed acceptance criteria or expressly reproduce “to the SFC’s satisfaction.” Without the relevant request, this paragraph’s conditional expectation is not triggered; that does not decide requirements arising elsewhere.
missing_premises: An applicable request for a legal opinion supporting the identified application.
The opinion’s required scope and applicable satisfaction criteria.
Evidence that an opinion meeting those criteria was obtained.
claims.proposition: Paragraph 16 separately concerns obtaining a satisfactory legal opinion supporting the application upon SFC request.

support.quote: Product Providers should, upon SFC’s request, obtain satisfactory legal opinion to support its application.

rival_readings: A — Main-text reading: demonstration is request-triggered and must satisfy the SFC concerning paragraph 14’s three subjects; the footnote’s precise integration remains unresolved.

B — Standing-footnote reading: footnote 5 independently expects confirmation and demonstration of its minimum content without a request. Its textual support is the unqualified wording, but it must account for paragraph 14’s express request condition.

C — Integrated reading: footnote 5 supplies minimum content for confirmation and request-triggered demonstration; paragraph 14 supplies the demonstration trigger and SFC-satisfaction standard. This is the more coherent textual reconciliation, offered as interpretive judgment rather than established legal correctness.
unresolved: The retained passages do not conclusively resolve the rival trigger readings or fully specify confirmation sufficiency, SFC satisfaction or high confidence.
Actual applicability, Product Provider status, request scope and timing, and performance facts are absent.
The provisions use “should”; their wording alone does not establish every legal consequence of noncompliance.

Candidate Boolean readings represent trigger differences only: identical A and C Boolean results do not establish identical objects or standards. Solver acceptance cannot establish legal truth or fulfillment.
